- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially after sharp price spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- Underestimate in the final 5–10 days of the forecast; adjust upward by 1–3% to align with recent mean reversion trends.
- Model tends to overreact to recent volatility; dampen forecast momentum after a 10%+ price spike.
- Forecast mean is consistently 1–3% higher than true outcome; apply a 1–2% downward bias to all forecasts.
- Lagged price movements (e.g., 3–5 day delays) are over-predicted; adjust forecasts to reflect 1–2 day lag in true price momentum.
- Avoid extrapolating from recent high volatility; use 30-day rolling average as a baseline for smoothing.
